extra.message: POST /api/auth/driver-access-assistance validates that licenceNumber was supplied but never compares it with the stored licence. Any nonempty value obtains a worker JWT when the supplied email identifies an enabled worker with an onboarding licence.

GET /api/customers/search interpolates both q and sort into SQL passed to sql.raw(). A dispatcher can inject SQL through the search literal or ORDER BY expression and access unauthorized database data.

POST /api/jobs/advanced-search constructs SQL clauses from request-body property names and values without escaping or parameterization. The resulting dsql.raw() query permits SQL injection by dispatchers.

The manifest lookup route interpolates x-shipment-code into a predicate that this helper compiles with new Function and executes for each shipment. A user with access to a populated route, including its field worker, can break out of the string and execute JavaScript in the server process.

POST /api/reports/quote-preview compiles customFormula from the query string with new Function and immediately invokes it when contractType is unknown. A dispatcher can execute arbitrary server-side JavaScript.

The statement-convert endpoint interpolates the unvalidated format query parameter into a shell command passed to execAsync(). A dispatcher with access to a customer can supply shell metacharacters or command substitutions to execute operating-system commands.

GET /api/reports/render embeds the template query parameter in a command subsequently executed by spawn() with shell:true. Quoting the title does not prevent command substitution, and the template path is unquoted. Dispatchers can execute arbitrary shell commands.

POST /api/data/archive/route/:id joins the caller-controlled tag to ARCHIVE_DIR and writes the result without a containment check. A tag containing ../ can create or overwrite accessible .csv files outside the archive directory.

The statement-layout endpoint joins the layout query parameter to STATEMENT_LAYOUT_DIR, reads the resulting file, and returns its contents. An ops admin can use ../ to read accessible .html files outside the intended layout directory.

The training endpoint joins the decoded courseName route parameter to TRAINING_MATERIALS_DIR without checking containment. A dispatcher can use encoded traversal components to read accessible .pdf files outside the training library.

Carrier manifest parsing resolves attacker-supplied SYSTEM entity paths using fs.readFileSync(). A user with route access can upload XML declaring a local file entity and reference it inside an item's code; the carrier-manifest/items endpoint returns the file contents.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: replyStagerWidget interpolates stored message bodies into raw HTML and an inline onclick handler. Its output reaches v-html at line 210. Customers and workers can submit messages containing injected elements or event handlers that execute in another job viewer's browser and access their localStorage JWT.

The incident summary is HTML-escaped but then embedded inside a JavaScript string in an onclick attribute and rendered with v-html. Browsers decode entities such as ' before compiling the handler, allowing a stored summary to escape the JavaScript string. A customer or worker can supply customerSummary when reporting an incident and execute script when staff click Copy summary.

GET /api/kiosk/route-preview-tile fetches kiosk_map_provider directly from an attacker-supplied Cookie header and returns the response body. No authentication, destination restriction, or redirect validation is applied, allowing unauthenticated requests to internal HTTP services.

Webhook URLs supplied through the admin API receive only generic URL validation before being fetched here. An ops admin can register and test URLs targeting loopback or private-network services; redirects are also followed without destination validation.

The recursive merge follows inherited target properties without rejecting __proto__. Any authenticated user can submit JSON through x-board-preferences to /api/board-preferences/sync; a nested __proto__ object reaches Object.prototype and modifies properties inherited throughout the server process.

cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes

extra.message: The unauthenticated legacy manifest-export endpoint explicitly skips signature verification. An attacker can base64url-encode arbitrary routeId, carrierAccountId, and future exp claims to retrieve another route's shipment references and statuses without a valid export link.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: Scoped carrier bearer tokens consist only of cps- followed by an incrementing counter. Attackers can enumerate active session identifiers and impersonate other carrier accounts without their credentials.

cwe: CWE-340: Generation of Predictable Numbers or Identifiers

extra.message: Legacy carrier sessions have no expiration field, and resolution accepts them for the process lifetime. No code revokes entries from portalSessions; the sign-out endpoint only removes scoped sessions. A stolen legacy token therefore retains access indefinitely until process restart.

The passphrase-change endpoint requires retireOtherDevices:true but only updates the password hash and records that flag. It never removes other account sessions, so previously issued bearer tokens remain usable despite the explicitly requested device revocation.

Password changes and resets update passwordHash without invalidating existing JWTs. authenticate() checks the account's existence and disabled flag but has no token version or password-change timestamp check. A stolen JWT remains usable for its original 12-hour lifetime after the victim changes or resets their password.

Badge-in upgrades the existing anonymous kiosk session in place without rotating its identifier. Someone who retains the terminal's pre-login token can reuse it after a worker badges in and perform authenticated job synchronization as that worker.

The kiosk session cookie is issued without HttpOnly or Secure and later becomes an authenticated worker credential. It is accessible to browser scripts and eligible for transmission over HTTP. The regenerated authenticated cookie at line 91 also omits Secure, even in production.

cwe: CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without HttpOnly Flag
CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without Secure Attribute

extra.message: Both kiosk synchronization handlers accept the stored workerId without rechecking whether the worker is disabled or still has the field-worker role. getKioskSession() also never checks createdAt. Captured sessions remain usable after account revocation or the hardened cookie's advertised 12-hour lifetime.

The badge-in continuation endpoint redirects directly to the next_screen cookie without validating the destination. The boot endpoint accepts and stores arbitrary nextScreen values, allowing a manipulated kiosk configuration to redirect users to an attacker-controlled external site.

Kiosk synchronization merges every request-body property into an assigned job and persists the result, removing only id. A field worker can change staff-controlled customerId, locationId, regionId, assignedWorkerId, routeId, serviceTypeId, and status fields.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The sync-safe endpoint accepts any job-status enum value and writes it without canTransitionJob() or the required-proof check. An assigned worker can mark a job completed without proof, skip mandatory intermediate states, or reopen terminal jobs. The unrestricted sync endpoint has the same workflow bypass.

cwe: CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow

extra.message: GET /api/jobs/messages/:messageId selects a message solely by its numeric ID and returns its body and sender. It never checks access to the associated job or customerVisible, allowing any authenticated account to enumerate other customers' messages and internal notes.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: GET /api/jobs/:id/messages uses the caller-controlled sharingMode query parameter to decide whether to filter internal messages. A customer or worker with job access can specify sharingMode=full to retrieve staff-only messages.

The job-detail endpoint filters internal messages only for customers. Assigned field workers receive the complete message collection, although canSeeInternal() excludes field workers and the scoped message endpoint hides these messages from them.

POST /api/jobs/draft-resume spreads attacker-supplied JSON directly into a job insert. Dispatchers can set normally server-controlled fields such as id, reference, status, assignedWorkerId, and routeId, including creating completed jobs without required proof.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The draft-resume-safe handler validates field types but never authorizes customerId, locationId, or regionId, nor checks that the location belongs to the customer. A region-scoped dispatcher can create jobs in another region or attach another customer's location to an accessible job, exposing that location through job detail.

The route-sheet-correction handler copies every request-body property into a database update after checking only access to the original job. Dispatchers can alter ownership, region, worker assignment, identifiers, and status, bypassing normal assignment, scope, and completion-proof checks.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The parameterized advanced-search-safe query applies only caller-selected filters and omits the authenticated dispatcher's region restriction. An empty filter returns jobs across all regions; a caller can explicitly request another region. The unsafe advanced-search handler also lacks this authorization constraint.

The customer list returns every customer to region-scoped dispatchers without applying regionId. Customer detail and both directory-search handlers likewise omit region authorization, exposing out-of-region contact details and, through detail, service locations despite getAccessibleCustomer() enforcing this boundary elsewhere.

POST /api/customers/:id/locations permits dispatchers to insert locations for any customerId without checking customer access or region. A dispatcher can create records under another region's customer by changing the path ID.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Customer creation accepts the submitted regionId without comparing it with the dispatcher's permitted region. Region-scoped dispatchers can create customer records in other regions. The CSV customer import in routes/data.ts also trusts the submitted region_code without enforcing dispatcher scope.

Normal job creation checks the submitted job region and that locationId belongs to customerId, but never authorizes access to that customer. A scoped dispatcher can use an out-of-region customer's location while assigning the new job their own region, gaining access to the linked customer and location through job detail.

POST /api/routes inserts the supplied regionId and workerId after only a staff-role check. A region-scoped dispatcher can create routes in arbitrary regions and assign them to arbitrary existing users without enforcing the permitted-region boundary.

Route detail authorizes a worker against route.workerId, then returns every linked job with complete customer and location records without checking job.assignedWorkerId. Route assignment and job assignment are independent, so workers can read jobs assigned to others, bypassing the per-job access restriction.

GET /api/data/export/incidents exports all incidents without joining jobs or filtering by the dispatcher's region. A scoped dispatcher can download titles and customer summaries for incidents that the incident list and detail endpoints deny them.

GET /api/admin/audit returns complete audit records to dispatchers without region or entity-access filtering. Incident updates store internalNotes in audit detail, so a region-scoped dispatcher can read another region's internal incident notes through this endpoint despite incident-detail authorization.

GET /api/reports/regional-summary is registered without authentication, and the report plugin has no global authentication hook. Anyone can retrieve organization-wide regional job counts and service-credit financial totals.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: All four legacy/widget routes are registered without authentication and return recent job references, statuses, and priorities across the organization. Framing and CORS headers do not authenticate callers; unauthenticated clients can read these operational records directly.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Carrier route queries use routes.name = routes.name rather than restricting rows to the authenticated carrier. Both route endpoints and both capacity endpoints share this flaw. Anyone can self-register a carrier account and retrieve other carriers' routes, worker assignments, and schedules.

Both carrier logo-upload endpoints lack authentication and account-ownership checks. An unauthenticated caller can upload for any existing accountId; the legacy endpoint uses a predictable accountId-based filename, allowing replacement of an existing carrier logo. The safe variant still permits unauthenticated writes to server storage.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Legacy carrier registration stores passwords as a single unsalted SHA-256 digest, and legacy login verifies the same digest. A database disclosure enables fast offline password guessing and recognition of shared passwords.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: Background-check submissions store full SSNs and driving-licence numbers directly in plaintext database columns. Database or backup access exposes these sensitive identity documents without an additional cryptographic boundary.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: If COMPLIANCE_DATA_KEY_HEX is absent or has the wrong length, bank-account encryption silently uses SHA-256 of the public constant local-dev-only-key. The fallback is not restricted to development. Anyone obtaining stored ciphertext, IV, and tag can decrypt payout accounts in such deployments.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: Missing MANIFEST_EXPORT_SIGNING_KEY silently selects a public hardcoded HMAC key in every environment. Attackers can sign arbitrary route and expiry claims accepted by the current manifest-export endpoint, bypassing its otherwise enabled signature verification.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: The integration API accepts the public constant demo-integration-key whenever INTEGRATION_API_KEY is unset, including outside development. Knowing this fallback lets an attacker retrieve and change job records through the status endpoint without a user account.

Password recovery logs the complete reset token and account email at info level without a development-only guard. Anyone with access to application logs can redeem the token at reset-password during its one-hour lifetime and take over the account.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The failed-onboarding endpoint logs the entire submitted request body. A submission containing a password but failing another field's validation stores that plaintext password and contact information in application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Carrier-rate exceptions return the raw server error stack to any authenticated account, including self-registered customers. The carrier-health endpoint also exposes stack and error details whenever the caller supplies any x-ops-console-session value. Upstream failures reveal internal paths and integration details.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Invoice acknowledgement sends the billing API key and invoice reference in a URL query string, using an HTTP endpoint by default. Network observers can capture the credential on the default transport, and URL logging at the receiving service or intermediaries can retain the key even when HTTPS is configured.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
CWE-598: Use of HTTP Request With Sensitive Query String

extra.message: POST /api/reports/digest accepts an unbounded routeIds array and performs an authorization query plus an unbounded stop query for every entry, retaining every result. Repeating one accessible route ID many times within the 2 MB body limit amplifies a single dispatcher request into hundreds of thousands of database operations and potentially very large responses.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: CSV escaping handles delimiters and quotes but leaves formula-leading characters unchanged. Customer-controlled incident titles and summaries reach the incident CSV export, allowing an attacker to place spreadsheet formulas in files opened by staff.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: The manifest scan-resume endpoint decrypts attacker-supplied unauthenticated AES-CBC ciphertext and returns distinguishable responses for padding failures versus other failures. This exposes a padding oracle that permits adaptive recovery of encrypted cursor plaintext. Route authorization is checked afterward and does not eliminate the oracle.

Missing or incorrectly sized MANIFEST_CURSOR_KEY_HEX selects a publicly derivable constant key without an environment restriction. Both CBC and GCM cursors can then be decrypted and forged by clients, defeating cursor confidentiality and integrity. The subsequent route authorization check still limits which routes can be accessed.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: The integration status endpoint checks the state transition but omits the service type's requiresProof check. An integration-key holder can move an in-progress job to completed without uploading proof, bypassing the completion requirement enforced by the normal job-status endpoint.

cwe: CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow

extra.message: Arrival confirmation writes status=arrived for any job assigned to the worker without checking its current state. A worker can reopen completed or cancelled jobs and bypass the fixed transition rules enforced by the normal status endpoint.

cwe: CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow

extra.message: Job creation never checks customer.creditHoldActive before inserting a new job. The credit-hold endpoint sets this flag specifically to stop new work, but normal creation, draft resume, and CSV job import all ignore it, allowing dispatchers to continue creating jobs after an admin places the account on hold.

cwe: CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow

extra.message: The login endpoint performs password verification on every request without an attempt counter, throttling, or lockout, and no global rate limiter is registered. Attackers can make unrestricted password guesses against known accounts; carrier and kiosk credential endpoints likewise lack attempt limits.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: The seed script provisions all demo users, including ops_admin, with the hardcoded password Passw0rd!, which the login page also publishes. Any installation retaining these seeded accounts permits login with publicly known credentials.
